subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION exception condition is set to exist'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 4). Expected behavior: 0 ** 0 under standard-binary sets EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION (level-3, Fatal per Table 14 / §14.7.5's no-phrase rule 1: 'if the rules for evaluation of exponentiation are violated'). READ: the exception EXISTS and the shape is implemented for the OTHER two modes -- CobolDec.Pow (CobolDec.cs:94-112) raises EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION on a zero base with a non-positive exponent, its message citing 'ISO §8.8.1.2 r6a / §8.8.1.5.4 r4' (CobolDec.cs:106), and on a negative base with a noninteger exponent citing §8.8.1.2 r6c (CobolDec.cs:112); the native twin is CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs (CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs:157/161, §8.8.1.2 rules 6a/6c). NEITHER cites §8.8.1.4.4 rule 4 and neither is reachable under standard-binary: CobolDec.Pow is reached only via NumericRenderer.Power's `if (StandardDecimal)` arm (NumericRenderer.cs:552), and StandardDecimal excludes ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary (NumericRenderer.cs:559). Upstream, DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOL0806 for the mode. So the SBIDI rule has no implementation -- a sibling rule of the same SHAPE is implemented for a different mode, which is precisely the case ground rule 5 says must not be stretched into CONFORMS. IMPLEMENTOR-LATITUDE CONTEXT (validated, and the reason this row is closable by decision as well as by code): `cite.py --check F.2 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements except for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent'` -> OK, and Annex A.3 item 2 (spec line 34878) reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor', with §4.2.6 (spec line 2137, validated by reading the clause heading at line 2135) making the claim decision the implementor's discretion, requiring only that the absence be documented and that a compile-time warning mechanism indicate the unsupported use -- both of which the repo already does (CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2, 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed'; COBOL0806 is the compile-time indication, and §4.2.6 explicitly does not require executable code). Ground rule 6 forbids me from awarding that disposition, so the verdict stays NOT-IMPLEMENTED and the disposition is surfaced as an owner decision. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation; not from ConstructRegistry). || REFUTED (code-location changed, with evidence): the adjudicator filed this row against `src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolDec.cs#Pow`, a symbol that implements a DIFFERENT clause for a DIFFERENT mode -- its own message text cites §8.8.1.2 r6a / §8.8.1.5.4 r4, i.e. the standard-DECIMAL twin -- and that is unreachable under standard-binary by the adjudicator's own reading. Naming it as this rule's location makes a NOT-IMPLEMENTED row look like it has an implementation site. Corrected to `src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/Emit/NumericRenderer.cs#Power`, the ONE exponentiation dispatch (line 543) whose two arms are `if (StandardDecimal)` (:551, StandardDecimal = {StandardDecimal, Standard} at :394) and the native default -- the site where a standard-binary arm, and with it rule 4's 0**0 leg, is missing. That is consistent with rows GR-8.8.1.4.4-1..-3 and with feedback_two_arm_dispatch. || REFUTED (the §4.2.6 defense is overstated): the note asserts 'COBOL0806 is the compile-time indication' satisfying §4.2.6. I read §4.2.6 in full (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:2135-2141): 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism at compile time to indicate use of syntactically-detectable processor-dependent language elements not supported by that implementation. Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax.' COBOL0806 discharges that ONLY for a program-definition or function-definition. §10.6.1 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:11028-11207) prints `[ options-paragraph ]` in the class-definition, factory-definition, instance-definition, interface-definition and method-definition skeletons too, and §11.2.1 (:11319-11337) repeats it after all seven id paragraphs -- but src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:92-94 reaches `identificationParagraph` (:153) -> `optionsParagraph` (:169) ONLY from programIdParagraph/functionIdParagraph, and Core/CobolOO.g4's classDefinition (:18), factoryParagraph (:31), objectParagraph (:52), interfaceDefinition (:72) and methodDefinition (:81) have no such production. In those five source-unit kinds `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` therefore produces exactly the bare syntax error §4.2.6 says the mechanism is NOT permitted to substitute for identifying the element. The latitude argument still stands for programs and functions; it does not yet stand for the compilation group as a whole, so the disposition is not as close to closable-by-decision as the note claims. Verdict unchanged: NOT-IMPLEMENTED (ground rule 6 -- documented-non-support is not mine to award, and support is absent). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
